haiku-low.q1: Keys load in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz cannot pass until the load succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the load 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving; customers see no errors.
haiku-low.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes and swaps in changed value and version pairs atomically. If a read fails, it keeps last good values, logs a warning, and retries next tick.
haiku-low.q4: In each process's in-memory cache as {name: (value, version_id)}. Never on disk, in environment variables, or in logs.
haiku-low.q5: orders-api-prod has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. The security on-call is the only writer. Engineers have no access.
haiku-low.q6: Old values stay in git history, which is not rewritten, so they count as leaked. Revoking old keys at the provider makes them harmless.
haiku-low.q7: Clients call secrets.get(name) on every request and put the value in the Authorization header, so a refreshed key is used from the next request.
haiku-low.q8: After the wait, check /healthz on every pod. All 4 must show the new version id before the old key is revoked.
haiku-low.q9: Set access; copy keys to store; one merge switches app to store and removes keys from config; then rotate at providers.
haiku-low.q10: From orders-api/dev/* in the secret store, using the developer's own login. make run sets APP_ENV=dev.
haiku-low.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, then exits non-zero, so the pod never becomes ready.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded in main before the HTTP server starts listening, so /healthz (readiness) cannot pass until the load succeeds.
sonnet.q2: After 3 retries 2 seconds apart, it logs the error (secret names only) and exits non-zero; it never becomes ready. The rollout halts and the old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes; if a version id changed, the new (value, version_id) pair replaces the old entry in one assignment. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value for each unreadable secret, updates the ones it could read, logs a warning (name and error, no value), retries at the next tick, and stays running and ready.
sonnet.q4: In an in-memory cache in each process, {name: (value, version_id)}. They must never be written to disk, environment variables or logs.
sonnet.q5: Read: orders-api-prod (read-only, only orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: The old values remain in git history, which is not being rewritten, so they count as leaked. They are made harmless by rotating each key at the provider (new key created, stored, confirmed on all pods) and then revoking the old key.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key at build time. On every outgoing call they call secrets.get("<name>") and put the value in the Authorization header, so the refreshed key is used from the next request with no restart.
sonnet.q8: After writing the new value, wait for the refresh (at most 5 minutes, allow 10), then check /healthz on every pod; all 4 must show the new version id. Only then revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access (and test it); 2) copy keys into the store; 3) one merge that switches the app to read from the store and removes the api_key lines from config/app.yaml (plus CI check); 4) verify; 5) rotate keys at providers one at a time (payments, email, geocoding); 6) retire pre-migration images.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store at orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), with APP_ENV=dev set by make run, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It does not start with a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 seconds apart; if it still fails it logs the error (names only) and exits with a non-zero code, never becoming ready.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Security has not decided whether or how often; the plan covers only the one-time rotation in step 5.
